style: Say brightly and clearly, like an upbeat tour guide
lines: Welcome, museum crew! Our hallway is going to be a museum. Tap a theme, then tap a piece to look closer.
Drag each piece onto the wall. Then tap the home it needs.
Opening day! Tap a job: Curator, Guard, Guide or Visitor.
Why does it belong in our museum? Tap a reason.
Five pieces! Tap Set up to build the museum.
Now slide it up or down. Tap Kid eyes to see what a kindergartner sees.
Tap Low, Middle or Tall to set the height. Tap Kid eyes to see what a kindergartner sees.
This is what kid eyes see. Tap a blurry piece, then change its height to make it clear.
Ready for opening day! Tap Opening day.
The hallway has five spots. Tap Back to cart, then a spot card and Put back.
Tap an empty bay to place this piece. Tap a filled bay to swap it.
Tap a piece to look closer. Pick five pieces for our museum.
Tap a home for this piece. Then set its height.
Tap Back to cart to choose another piece, or tap another reason.
Tap Yes, start over to clear the museum, or Keep it to keep your work.
Tap Pick it to add this artwork, or Back to cart to look at another.
Tap Back to cart, then Set up to build our museum. Or tap another reason.
Tap Up or Down, or drag the piece. Tap Check the hallway when you are ready.
Tap Low, Middle or Tall. Tap Check the hallway when you are ready.
Look at the three badges in each row. Tap Back to wall to make a change.
Tap a tray piece to select it. Change its home or height, then tap Check the hallway.
Tap a tray piece first. Then tap this bay.
This bay is empty. Tap Next piece to find art, or tap Choose to pick art.
Act out this job. Tap Next prompt for another idea.
Back on the cart. Tap Pick it to choose it again, or Back to cart.
Tap an artwork to look closer. Your five picks stay when the theme changes.
Flat paper art hangs flat. Try a Frame.
This piece is not flat. Try a Stand or a Glass case.
It is small and could fall or break. A Glass case keeps it safe.
It is too big for the case. Try a Stand.
It hangs and moves. Try a Wall rod.
Light can't shine through it here. Try the window.
It blocks the window light. Try another bay.
Too high for kid eyes. Slide it down.
Too low. Slide it up.
Too low for kid eyes. Tap Tall, or try Middle.
Does this fit our theme? Tell why, or choose another piece.
Pick a home.
Tap a tray piece, then tap this bay.
A Glass case is also fine.
All three checks. Ready to show!
Fox in the Snow. It is made of tempera paint on paper.
Clay Turtle. It is made of clay, painted.
Yarn Rainbow. It is made of yarn woven on a stick.
Sunflower Collage. It is made of torn paper glued on card.
Little Clay Pot with a Sprout. It is made of clay, painted.
Cardboard Robot. It is made of boxes, tubes, bottle caps.
Rain Puddles. It is made of watercolor on paper.
Ladybug Rocks. It is made of painted rocks.
Caterpillar to Butterfly. It is made of paper circles on a string.
Tissue Paper Tree. It is made of tissue paper on clear plastic.
Rocket Ship. It is made of crayon on paper.
Snowman Sculpture. It is made of cotton balls on a cardboard tube.
Curators choose the art. Tell the visitors our theme.
Point to one piece. Tell why we chose it.
Guards keep the art safe. Show the rules: walk, look with your eyes, hands to yourself.
Someone is running in the museum! Show what a guard says.
Guides tell visitors about the art. Tell one thing you see in the glowing piece.
Tell what it is made of, and how you think the artist made it.
Visitors look closely. Look at the glowing piece for five quiet seconds.
Ask the guide one question. Then tell which piece you like best, and why.
This is the lowest height. Tap Up, or drag the piece higher. Tap Check the hallway when you are ready.
This is the highest height. Tap Down, or drag the piece lower. Tap Check the hallway when you are ready.
